# HCopyField

> A read-only endpoint, identifier, or secret field with explicit clipboard and reveal actions.

[Start with the Hearth UI agent index](../../../llms.txt). This describes repository source for version 0.4.0. Match documentation to your installed source/release.

## Identity

- Vue export: `HCopyField` from `@hearth-ui/vue`.
- Custom element: `<hearth-copy-field>`.
- Constructor: `HearthCopyFieldElement` from `@hearth-ui/elements`.
- Category: Controls.
- [Implementation](https://github.com/samishal1998/hearth-ui/blob/main/src/components/HCopyField.vue).

## Choose and use it correctly

- This is a read-only display/copy field, not an editable form field.
- secret masks the display and offers explicit reveal; masking does not protect the value from the consuming application or browser tools.
- Clipboard failures are visible and emitted. The user can select/copy manually; successful copying emits no secret value.

## Public API

label, value: string · secret, disabled: boolean

A `?` marks optional source props. Props with defaults may be omitted. Internal `formDisabled` and `control-sync` plumbing is excluded below; do not use it in application code.

```ts
type Props = {
    label: string;
    value: string;
    secret?: boolean;
    disabled?: boolean;
};
```

### Defaults

No component defaults; optional props are undefined (absent boolean props cast to false unless explicitly defaulted).

### Events

copied(), copy-error(message)

```ts
type Emits = {
    copied: [
    ];
    "copy-error": [
        message: string
    ];
};
```

Vue-emitted custom-element events expose argument arrays in `event.detail`. Listen on the element. Native events such as `click` retain their normal payloads. The elements package provides framework-independent DOM event types.

### Slots

None

Vue uses `<template #slotName>`; custom elements use `<div slot="slotName">`. Web components do not support Vue scoped slots.

### CSS parts

base, label, value

Use `hearth-copy-field::part(part-name)` for an exposed part or inherited `--h-*` tokens for shared styling. Native Vue components use the shared stylesheet and `h-*` classes.

## Vue example

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import { HCopyField } from '@hearth-ui/vue';
import '@hearth-ui/vue/styles.css';

</script>

<template>
  <HCopyField label="Service endpoint" value="https://photos.example.com" />
</template>
```

## Web-component example

Provide a mount point. For field submission, use an owning native form; the auth page already contains its own form.

```html
<div id="example"></div>
```

This is bundler-based ESM. For raw HTML, load `dist/themes.css` with a link and import `registerElements` from `./dist/elements/index.js` instead. Initial array/object properties are assigned before connection to establish reset defaults.

```js
import { registerElements } from '@hearth-ui/elements';
import '@hearth-ui/elements/themes.css';
registerElements();

const mount = document.querySelector('#example');
const element = document.createElement('hearth-copy-field');
Object.assign(element, {
  "label": "Service endpoint",
  "value": "https://photos.example.com"
});

mount.append(element);
```
